newsitem.title: USA: Bank reform to expand Federal Home Loan banks.
newsitem.headline: Bank reform to expand Federal Home Loan banks.

text.p: The House Banking Committee voted on Thursday to amend financial sector reform legislation to expand the lending authority of Federal Home Loan Banks into agricultural and small-business loans.

The amendment, sponsored by Louisiana Republican Richard Baker, would also make membership in the Home Loan system voluntary. In the current system, savings and loans institutions are required to be members.
Home Loan Bank system members with less than $500 million of assets would be authorized to use advances for small-business, agricultural, rural development and low-income development lending.

The controversial expansion of loan authority had been included in earlier drafts of the reform bill but was removed when some lawmakers said private-sector agricultural lenders would face unfair competition.
But the committee's chairman Jim Leach, Republican of Iowa, said the greater competition would benefit agricultural and small-business lenders.
"This increases the availability of credit in the agricultural community dramatically," Leach said.

The amendment would alter the system's capital structure to account for the loss of mandatory members. Risk-based capital rules would be applied to each Home Loan Bank. The amendment also would make it easier for banks with less than $500 million in assets to join the system.

The banking committee is in its third day of debate over bank reform legislation. The Home Loan provision could be changed or removed as the bill moves forward. If the committee approves a bill, the legislation next moves to the Commerce Committee for further consideration.
